text:
Maria: Heads-up — multiple support tickets reporting p99 latency ~1.6s after today's runtime rollout to canary. Customers acme + buddy impacted. Anyone else seeing this?

Kevin: Yep, saw perf alerts. p95 jumped 120ms -> 380ms, p99 420ms -> ~1600ms on canary hosts. Alert fired at 09:12UTC.

Maria: Timeline matches: roll started 09:08, finished canary batch ~09:10. Graph: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/latency/canary (share).

Jen: Can you paste the PromQL or query and cohort filter you used?

Maria: Query: `sum by(route)(histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))`
Filter: `tenant_id=~"(acme|buddy)"`

Eli: Logs show TLS handshakes spiking and some `connection reset by peer`. sample lines: `time=09:12:21 lvl=warn msg="tls: handshake took 312ms" route=/v1/generate`, `time=09:12:23 lvl=info msg="write slow: 200ms" err="write: broken pipe"`

Maria: Looking at canary sidecar config diff from rollout:
```diff
- tcp_keepalive_interval: 60s
+ tcp_keepalive_interval: 1s
- connection_pool:
-   max_idle: 100
+ connection_pool:
+   max_idle: 50
```
Not sure if that change came from runtime or sidecar image bump.

Kevin: There was also a kernel tune pushed to canary nodes earlier: `net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1` and `net.ipv4.tcp_tw_recycle=1` flipped on. That can make ephemeral port reuse noisier with short keepalives.

oncall-bot: Incident created INC-2026-324 and notified oncall. Assigned to Kevin.

Jen: Proposed bisect plan: compare runtime+sidecar combo v2.8.0 (canary) vs v2.7.3 (stable). Steps: 1) divert 30% of suspect cohort off canary -> measure 5m p99 2) rollback sidecar config on one canary pool 3) revert kernel tweak on one node pool -> isolate culprit.

Maria: I diverted 30% of acme/buddy traffic to stable at 09:22. Metrics after 5m: p95 improved to ~160ms, p99 to ~480ms (still above baseline but much better). So routing helps.

Eli: Runbook check: CPU/mem/IO on canary hosts normal. This looks connection/handshake related, not queueing. Repro script I used:
```bash
# simple load repro (run from k8s job)
hey -c 50 -z 2m "https://api.redwood/v1/generate?tenant=acme" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' --keepalive=true
```
I see a subset of requests with `tls: handshake took >200ms` and transient `connection reset by peer`.

Kevin: Temporary mitigation: 1) increase `connection_pool.max_idle` to 200 on canary sidecars 2) set `tcp_keepalive_interval` back to 60s 3) revert tcp_tw_recycle on a node-pool. If metrics look stable, roll to remaining canaries.

support-bot: Notified affected customers that we're investigating and have routed traffic to reduce impact. (Ticket references attached).

Maria: Actioned: updated sidecar pool size on 12 canary hosts at 09:30 and reverted keepalive to 60s on those hosts. After 10m p95 ~140ms p99 ~450ms. Partial fix but some tail remains.

Jen: I'll take the bisect on the sidecar commits. Kevin, can you coordinate kernel revert on a small node-pool and report perf delta? Eli, keep running repro and collect packet traces if tail persists.

Eli: Will collect `tcpdump` + `strace` on the repro node. If we see SYN+RST patterns or client-side timeouts that'll point at ephemeral port exhaustion or aggressive keepalive resets.

Kevin: Preparing rollback plan in case root cause is runtime image: full canary rollback to v2.7.3 + sidecar pinned at last-known-good. ETA for rollback window ~10m once approvals in #eng-sre.

Maria: Notes / next steps (short):
- Jen: bisect sidecar commits (owner)
- Kevin: kernel revert trial + rollback readiness (owner)
- Eli: repro + packet traces (owner)
- Maria: notify customers and draft postmortem skeleton

Jen: I'll create a PR linking bisect results and mark potential guilty commit if reproduced.

support-bot: Customer ACME updated: "we've routed some traffic to stable, investigating; will provide update in 30m"

Kevin: tagging @security because kernel param changes may have policy implications.

Maria: Thanks all. If tail drops below 600ms p99 in next 30m we consider canary stabilized; otherwise we trigger full rollback. :thumbsup:
